claims.statement: Tool calls from multiple accounts referenced the same artifact(s): domain:payroll-verify-portal.example, url:https://payroll-verify-portal.example/sso.
BEH-001 (Progressive intent escalation within a session) fired on 5 account(s).
BEH-002 (Reformulation immediately after refusal) fired on 5 account(s).
BEH-003 (Harmful workflow assembled from benign fragments) fired on 5 account(s).
BEH-004 (Obfuscation shift after boundary contact) fired on 2 account(s).
BEH-005 (Tool activity staging infrastructure alongside abusive content) fired on 5 account(s).
BEH-006 (Account re-registration after enforcement on a linked account) fired on 2 account(s).
The linked accounts are more consistent with a single operator than with independent users.
Activity resumed in a later wave from different network space after enforcement, with the same client fingerprint and reused artifact.
No identity attribution is made. Linkage supports an operator hypothesis only; shared infrastructure and phrasing do not establish who the operator is.

competing_explanations.hypothesis: Shared egress: unrelated users behind one VPN, campus, or office NAT.
competing_explanations.assessment: Weakened. Linkage does not rest on network prefix alone; strong identifiers present: client_fingerprint, payment_fingerprint, shared_artifact.

competing_explanations.hypothesis: Authorised security-awareness team producing phishing-simulation material.
competing_explanations.assessment: Weakened. Sessions show refusal-driven reformulation and euphemistic relabelling, which authorised training work does not require.

competing_explanations.hypothesis: Shared managed device pool, e.g. an agency using one browser image.
competing_explanations.assessment: Partially credible; a common browser image can duplicate a client fingerprint. It does not explain reuse of the same externally controlled artifact.

competing_explanations.hypothesis: Detection artefact: rules over-fire on the same benign template language.
competing_explanations.assessment: Weakened. Multiple independent rule families fired: BEH-001, BEH-002, BEH-003, BEH-004, BEH-005, BEH-006

evidence_gaps: Ownership of the shared artifact is unconfirmed; no registrar or hosting evidence is available from first-party telemetry.
No evidence shows that generated content was ever delivered to a recipient. Harm is potential, not observed.
Client fingerprints can be duplicated by a common browser image; treat as strong-but-not-unique.
Payment fingerprints differ between waves, so billing does not corroborate the link.
The gap between waves is unexplained; the operator may have been active on surfaces outside this telemetry.

recommended_actions.description: Suspend the accounts with direct high-severity evidence, with appeal path.
recommended_actions.rationale: Campaign confidence is 0.87 (high). 5 account(s) carry direct high-severity evidence, 0 are linked by association only. Action is scoped to the evidence tier held for each account.
recommended_actions.proportionality: Accounts linked only by weak correlates receive monitoring, not suspension.

recommended_actions.description: Add reused artifacts to the outbound-fetch watchlist and alert on new touches.
recommended_actions.rationale: The reused artifact is the most durable pivot across waves.
